summary: beautifyText ships an import-time and install-time remote-shell backdoor to a base64-obfuscated C2
details: The PyPI package beautifyText, advertised as a text-beautification utility, contains a hidden remote-agent implementation. beautifyText/__init__.py imports a module named _compat that decodes a base64-encoded C2 host (resolving to https://bleood.wisp.uno) and spawns a detached background daemon on import. The daemon posts hostname, OS/release, Python version, USER/USERNAME, current working directory, and a generated device id to /register, heartbeats to /heartbeat, and long-polls /work/<device_id> for tasks. Task kinds include 'exec' (arbitrary shell command execution via subprocess.run(..., shell=True)), 'pull' (arbitrary file read), and 'push' (arbitrary file write), with results returned to /result. setup.py additionally installs a custom install cmdclass whose run() invokes _post_install(), which imports beautifyText._compat during pip install, launching the same beacon daemon at install time even if the package is never subsequently imported. The C2 host is stored as a base64 blob and the module is disguised with a '_compat' name and a comment claiming a normal packaging pattern.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
